_README: Acknowledged drift for the per-subsystem security audits, checked by
frontend/scripts/check-audit-freshness.mjs (runs in `npm run check`).
An audit's `Audited commit` is the code state its claims were verified
against. When the content under that audit's `Code paths` moves away from
it, the check goes red. Two ways out, both legitimate:
1. Re-verify the audit -> bump `Audited commit` in the doc, add a change
log entry, and drop the audit's entry from this file.
2. Review the drift and conclude it cannot move a verdict -> record the
current object id of each `Code paths` entry in `reviewedTrees` and
say why in `note`.
What is NOT legitimate is recording an object id without reading the diff.
The note is the evidence that someone did.
`reviewedTrees` holds git object ids (a tree for a directory, a blob for a
file), not commit SHAs. Get them from the check itself: when it fails it
prints the current id of every path that moved, ready to paste.
Object ids rather than commit SHAs because this repo squash-merges. A SHA
written during a PR names the branch commit, which stops existing the
moment the PR lands — so the gate that was green locally went red on main
and needed a follow-up commit that changed nothing but a SHA. That cost six
fixes in the two days the SHA-based version existed. Squashing rewrites
history, not content, so an object id simply survives it, along with
rebases, cherry-picks and force pushes.

docs/IMAP_SMTP_AUDIT.md.note: Two commits reviewed. 4e3b223 changes which exception MailConnectionProbe throws when the server rejects a login: MailAuthenticationException instead of MailConnectionException, so the reply text stops being rendered into the user-facing error.mail.connectionFailed placeholder and travels as the cause into the log instead. That narrows what server-controlled text reaches the UI; it touches no TLS, auth-mechanism or timeout setting. Re-checked on the probe specifically: pinned ssl.checkserveridentity, the fail-closed OAuth2-requires-SSL guard and the millisecond-string timeouts are all unchanged. 5c76f91 adds an outbound content type: MimeMessageBuilder attaches a text/html alternative rendered by the new MarkdownBodyRenderer when the composed body uses Markdown. The HTML is generated locally from the user's own keystrokes, never from server-controlled data, so the hostile-server surface this boundary is about is untouched — as are TLS setup, auth mechanisms, timeouts, connection pooling and every IMAP command path. Re-checked the send path specifically: the CRLF guard on header-bound fields (requireSingleLine) and both AddressPolicy branches are unchanged, and drafts stay single-part text/plain, so the IMAP APPEND payload shape is identical to what was audited. The renderer runs with escapeHtml and sanitizeUrls on and HtmlBlock parsing off, so it cannot emit script, event handlers or non-http/mailto URLs; rendering is skipped above 512 kB, below the existing 10 MB body cap, so it adds no unbounded CPU sink to the send path. Verdict stays PASS. Third commit reviewed: the conversation-scope change adds FolderRole.SENT to CONVERSATION_EXCLUDED_ROLES in MailFacade, which under this path is two functional lines (the role list and a log string) plus javadoc. It moves nothing this boundary is about: no TLS setting, auth mechanism, timeout, connection-pool or IMAP command path is touched, and no server-controlled bytes are parsed differently — the change decides which folders a read-path query counts. Two effects re-checked because they do reach IMAP. (1) The listing now resolves a fourth folder role per page, through the same bounded findFolderNamesByRoleWithoutWaiting call the other three already used, with the same fail-closed handling: an unresolvable role still degrades the whole listing to folder-scoped rather than guessing an exclusion set. (2) The resolved names are attacker-controlled (the server names its folders) and now include the sent folder, but they ride the same :excludedFolders JPQL parameter binding as before, so the NOT IN clause gains a value, not a new injection surface; the list stays bounded by the folders the server reports for those roles, which was already true of trash, junk and drafts. Verdict stays PASS.

docs/UPDATER_AUDIT.md.note: c16b3df adds the tray icon, its menu and close-to-tray under frontend/src-tauri/src. The updater itself is untouched: endpoints, the embedded pubkey, check_for_update/install_pending_update and the expected-version pin on the pending slot are unchanged, as are tauri.conf.json (CSP, updater plugin config) and capabilities/default.json — the new commands are app-defined and therefore not capability-gated, and the tray is built Rust-side. New surface reviewed: three commands (configure_tray, set_tray_tooltip, set_close_behavior) that take only strings and a bool from the webview and reach nothing but tray label/tooltip APIs and an in-process Mutex<bool>; a CloseRequested handler that hides the main window; and a tray menu whose Quit calls the same app.exit(0) the window path already reaches. None of that touches signature verification or the download path, so the B6 verdict does not move. Flagged for the next full B6 pass rather than settled here: tauri-plugin-single-instance is a new supply-chain item (32 crates added to Cargo.lock) and opens a local IPC channel (a named object on Windows) that another process on the same machine can address — low risk under the single-user local threat model, but it is new attack surface under an audited path, not a reshuffle of existing code. cargo audit is clean after the change apart from the pre-existing allowed RUSTSEC-2026-0190 in anyhow. Re-reviewed for the follow-up fixes in the same paths: the CloseBehavior default flips to quitting, set_close_behavior refuses to enable hiding without a tray icon, and a failed tray build is logged rather than propagated out of setup. All three narrow what the shell does on a failure path and none of them touch the updater, the capability set or the CSP, so the verdict is unmoved.

docs/API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md.note: 3c2e1b3 touches this path in documentation only: ConversationSummaryResponse gains a reworded record javadoc and a reworded @Schema description for messageCount, because the conversation scope stopped spanning the sent folder. No field was added, removed, renamed or retyped, no nullability changed, and no validation annotation was touched — so none of the things this audit weighs (request-body bounds, DTO size limits, what the surface exposes) moved. Evidence rather than assertion: the golden api-docs.json diff for the commit is a single description string, and the schema.d.ts regenerated from it differs by exactly the one @description comment line that carries it — no type, field name or optionality in the generated client surface moves. Verdict stays PASS. — 9567d49 moves the address book out of the account scope: the contact endpoints go from /api/v1/accounts/{accountId}/contacts and .../contact-labels to /api/v1/contacts and /api/v1/contact-labels, and both controllers lose their accountId path variable (autocomplete keeps it as a @RequestParam @Positive). Nothing this audit weighs moves with them. Authorization is path-independent: SecurityConfig permits only PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS (the OAuth callbacks) and leaves anyRequest().authenticated() behind ApiKeyFilter, so a relocated path keeps the same posture — there is no per-prefix rule to fall out of. The two counts the enumeration rests on are unchanged (17 @RestController, 12 @Validated): no controller was added, removed, or stripped of @Validated. Every bound §2 cites is untouched — bulk 100 items, merge 9 sources / 10 emails, label assignment 100 contacts / 50 labels, label name 60 chars, contactQueryMaxLength and the contactAutocompleteMaxLimit clamp — and the whole contact/dto diff for this commit is a single javadoc line; account/dto only gains @Nullable on MailProviderResponse.oauth2RegistrationId, which springdoc does not read, so the golden api-docs.json does not move for it. Error hygiene is unchanged in shape: the contact exceptions drop their accountId argument and still resolve through AppException to an RFC 9457 ProblemDetail. The audit enumerates no endpoint paths, so the move leaves no stale claim. Verdict stays PASS.
